On October 16, 2026, Congress President and Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seeking an all-party meeting to discuss the government’s delimitation proposals before they were finalised and introduced in Parliament. It was Mr. Kharge’s fourth letter since April seeking such a meeting. On October 19, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju replied, saying that the government had repeatedly sought the Congress’s cooperation, including through letters to Mr. Kharge in March and April and discussions with him and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi.
Mr. Rijiju also said that the government had held consultations with several other Opposition parties. Yet, his reply showed once again that the Centre had no intention of disclosing its precise proposals on delimitation. Without explicitly saying so, Mr. Rijiju’s letter suggested that the government planned to bring in legislation on delimitation while withholding the details, thereby preventing a possible public debate on the issue.
